links.outcome: Flesch-Kincaid grade level of LLM responses versus recommended patient education reading level
links.effect: Both models' FKGL exceeded the sixth to eighth grade standard; Gemini responses were significantly longer and had higher FKGL than ChatGPT.
links.quote: However, readability scores (FKGL) for both models exceeded standards for patient education recommendations for sixth to eighth grade reading level or below suggesting there may be barrier to understandability for the general population.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated responses to parent questions relative to patient comprehension
links.effect: FKGL for both ChatGPT and Gemini exceeded the sixth to eighth grade level recommended for patient education, suggesting a barrier to understandability.
links.quote: However, readability scores (FKGL) for both models exceeded standards for patient education recommendations for sixth to eighth grade reading level or below suggesting there may be barrier to understandability for the general population.

screen.reason: The study evaluates the performance, safety, and readability of ChatGPT and Gemini on pediatric celiac disease questions using expert clinician reviewers, without testing a specific organizational deployment practice or guardrail.
